h1: NAS 410 Audit Compliance Documentation for Nadcap and Customer Audits
html:
Read this if you manage quality or NDT at an aerospace supplier, special-process house or repair station, a purchase order has invoked NAS 410, and an auditor (Nadcap's NDT Task Group, a prime's source team or the FAA) is due to look at your certification files. Atlantis prepares and reviews the documentation for those NAS 410 and Nadcap AC7114 audits, and your company's Responsible Level 3 approves it: the written practice, the personnel qualification files, the procedures and the evidence trail behind every certification. Send us the audit date and the methods in scope to start.

What Atlantis does and does not do for NAS 410 programmes

Atlantis is not your Responsible Level 3 and does not certify anyone to NAS 410. It delivers no NAS 410 training, and it does not write, administer or grade NAS 410 examinations. Under the standard, your company certifies its own NDT personnel under its written practice. Your Responsible Level 3, designated in writing by your company, approves that written practice, the procedures, the training and examination arrangements and any outside agency. Nothing Atlantis drafts takes effect until that person approves it.

The work Atlantis does sits around that authority. An ASNT NDT Level III compares your written practice and records with the NAS 410 revision your customers invoke and with the Nadcap AC7114 checklists, drafts or revises documents for the Responsible Level 3 to sign, sorts personnel files so each certification can be traced to its evidence, runs a mock audit, and helps you assemble corrective-action evidence after findings. Atlantis is not a Nadcap auditor, is not Nadcap-accredited, and holds no approval from any aerospace prime. Nobody at Atlantis holds a Level 3 certification issued under NAS 410; the company's Level III credentials are ASNT certifications.

That division matters at audit time. The auditor will ask who approved each document and on what authority, and the answer must always be your Responsible Level 3, not an outside consultant.

How NAS 410 certification looks to an auditor

NAS 410 is the Aerospace Industries Association standard for qualifying and certifying the people who perform NDT on aerospace hardware, and it is kept technically aligned with the European EN 4179. It binds a supplier through contracts and customer quality requirements rather than through regulation. It is also employer-based: no central US body certifies people to it. An auditor therefore looks for a closed loop inside your company:

  • a written practice, approved by the Responsible Level 3, saying how each method and level is trained, examined, certified and recertified;
  • formal training against an approved outline, delivered by a qualified instructor, with the hours recorded;
  • supervised experience in the method, logged as it was earned rather than reconstructed later;
  • near-vision and color-perception examinations, with near vision repeated at least every twelve months;
  • general, specific and practical examinations, graded under the written practice;
  • a certification issued by the employer for the method, level and techniques, for a period of no more than five years.

Certification is granted method by method and level by level, with Level 1 Limited, Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3 above the trainee stage, and the Responsible Level 3 holding overall authority for the programme. AIA and Accuris released Revision 6 in December 2025. Its headline change is a new Appendix D, a points route through which Level 2 personnel who complete designated NDT activities can become eligible for the initial Level 3 examination; AIA also describes the revision as strengthening and clarifying certification requirements. The background is in our NAS 410 explainer, and the differences from the ASNT recommended practice are set out in NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A.

Who audits a NAS 410 programme, and against what

Most aerospace NDT suppliers face more than one kind of audit, and each auditor reads the same records with a different checklist in hand.

AuditWho carries it outWhat they audit againstWhat they sample
Nadcap NDT accreditationAn auditor approved by the Nadcap NDT Task Group, with the programme administered by the Performance Review Institute (PRI)The AC7114 quality system checklist, a method slash sheet for each method held (for example AC7114/1 for penetrant, /2 magnetic particle, /3 ultrasonic, /4 film radiography, /5 eddy current), and the customer requirements you claim to meetIndividual certifications traced back to their evidence, and job audits that follow a real part from procedure to accept or reject
Prime or tier-one source auditThe customer's supplier quality or NDT specialistPurchase-order quality clauses, the customer's process specifications, and NAS 410 or EN 4179 as invokedWhether each customer addition has reached the documents your technicians work to
Repair station surveillanceFAA inspectors and the station's own customersThe 14 CFR Part 145 training programme; FAA Advisory Circular 65-31B lists NAS 410 among acceptable standards for NDI personnelWhether the station follows the standard its own manual names
Internal auditYour quality functionYour quality manual and written practiceEverything above, before anyone outside looks

Nadcap accredits special processes at a site; it does not certify people. Findings are raised as nonconformances that the supplier answers through PRI's eAuditNet system with containment, root cause, corrective action and evidence, and the Task Group reviews the responses before accreditation is granted. Our page on Nadcap AC7114 audit readiness explains why most of those findings land on records rather than on technique, and what Nadcap accreditation actually checks gives the supply-chain view.

The documents an auditor opens

This is the document set an NDT auditor works through in a NAS 410 programme, with the gap that turns up most often in each. It is also the order in which Atlantis reviews a file.

DocumentWhat the auditor checksCommon gap
Written practiceCites the standard and revision your customers invoke, covers every method and level you certify, names any outside agency, and carries the Responsible Level 3's dated approvalThe revision letter was updated but the content was not
Responsible Level 3 designationA written appointment by the company, the designee's Level 3 certification in each method they approve, and who handles technical approvals in the other methodsNo appointment letter, or a letter naming someone who has left
Outside agency agreementsA contract stating what the agency supplies and how the Responsible Level 3 controls itAn agency used for training or examinations but never named in the written practice
Training recordsCourse outline, instructor and the basis of their qualification, hours by method and level, dates and signaturesHours that meet the minimum with no outline behind them
Experience recordsHours in the method logged as earned and signed by the supervising Level 2 or Level 3A log written up in one sitting, one pen, one date
Examination recordsGeneral, specific and practical papers, graded, with question bank revision, practical specimen identity and examinerOnly the final score kept; specimen not identified
Vision recordsTest method, result, examiner and date for near vision and color perceptionNear-vision test lapsed while the person kept working
Certification recordsMethod, level, techniques, limitations, period and the employer's signatureOne certificate covering methods with no examination behind them
Recertification recordsThe route the written practice allows, and the evidence for itRecertified by signature alone
Instructor and examiner qualificationThe basis on which each instructor and examiner was approvedNothing on file beyond a name
NDT procedures and technique sheetsApproval by a Level 3 certified in the method, current customer specification references, revision controlA procedure citing a superseded customer specification
Interrupted serviceHow a gap in method use is tracked, and the evidence for reinstatementNo tracking at all
Records retentionA defined retention period that meets customer requirementsRetention never stated

Several of these record types have their own pages: examination records under AC7114, training records and certificates, experience logs, vision examination records and records retention for aerospace NDT.

Flowing prime requirements down into your documents

NAS 410 sets minimums. Primes and tier-one customers add their own requirements in purchase-order quality clauses and process specifications: more training hours for a method, particular examination content, customer approval of the supplier's Level 3, additional records, or a specific revision of the standard. An auditor checks that each addition reached the documents your technicians actually use.

A flow-down matrix is the simplest proof. Give each customer requirement one row, naming the purchase order or specification, the clause of your written practice, procedure or technique sheet that satisfies it, and the date that clause took effect. When a customer issues a new specification revision, the matrix shows at once which documents must change. Atlantis builds and reviews these matrices from the purchase orders and specifications you hold. It does not hold approvals from any prime, and it does not mark a customer requirement as met until your Responsible Level 3 and quality manager agree that it is.

Preparing your documentation for Revision 6

A revision change is where documentation drifts out of step. The written practice gets a new revision letter while training outlines, examination banks and certification forms keep referring to the old one, and the auditor finds the mismatch in minutes. A controlled transition usually covers these steps:

  1. Obtain Revision 6 from Accuris and list every change that touches your programme. Work from the standard itself; summaries, including ours, are not a substitute.
  2. Check what transition your customers have set. Customers and your written practice decide the timing, and earlier editions allowed existing certifications to run until they expired rather than forcing immediate recertification.
  3. Decide, through the Responsible Level 3, whether your company will use the Appendix D points route. If it will, design a record that shows points earned by activity category, signed off as they are earned.
  4. Update the written practice, training outlines, examination banks, certification forms and the flow-down matrix together, under one change record.
  5. Brief the people affected, and keep the superseded documents in your archive so certifications issued under the earlier revision can still be traced.

Atlantis can prepare the change record, the redlined written practice and the updated forms for approval, and can check them against the AC7114 quality system checklist before your next audit.

Cleaning up records without rewriting history

A gap review often shows that some certifications rest on incomplete evidence: a missing training outline, an experience log written up after the fact, a practical examination with no record of which specimen was used. Recreating the missing paper is never the answer. Auditors are good at spotting records produced in a batch, and a reconstructed record is a far more serious finding than an honest gap.

What Atlantis does instead is list each gap, tie it to the certification it affects, and lay out the options: retraining, re-examination, a limitation written onto the certification, or suspension until the evidence exists. The Responsible Level 3 chooses, and the decision is recorded with its reasoning. Where a finding has already been raised, the same record becomes part of the corrective action, as described in corrective action records for aerospace NDT. For keeping expiry dates under control afterwards, see catching technician certifications before they lapse and the certificate tracking app.

How an engagement runs

  1. Scope. You tell us which audit is coming, which methods and levels you certify, which customers invoke NAS 410 or EN 4179, and which revision each one names.
  2. Gap review. An ASNT NDT Level III checks the written practice, the NDT procedures and several complete personnel files against the invoked revision, the AC7114 quality system checklist, the slash sheet for each method and your customers' specifications, and returns a finding list ranked by audit risk.
  3. Drafting for approval. We draft or revise what is missing, ready for the Responsible Level 3 to approve: the written practice, a designation letter template, outside agency agreements, the training plan and course outline register, the procedure describing how your company administers and controls its own examinations, certification and recertification forms, the interrupted-service rule and the retention schedule. NDT procedures and technique sheets are prepared for approval by a Level 3 certified in the method; see NDT procedure development and written practices for aerospace NDT.
  4. Personnel files. We sort each person's training, experience, examination, vision and certification evidence into a consistent file and flag every gap for a decision.
  5. Mock audit. We walk the AC7114 checklist with your quality and NDT staff, then trace a real job: the part, the procedure revision used, the technician's certification and vision on that date, the equipment and material controls, and the accept or reject record. The checklist view is summarised in Nadcap AC7114 audit preparation.
  6. After the audit. We help you write root cause and corrective action for each nonconformance and assemble the objective evidence, so the responses you submit are complete the first time the Task Group reads them.

Document work runs remotely from Houston and Hyderabad. Mock audits and job traces are done on site at your facility. For wider support on aerospace programmes built on the ASNT document, see aerospace NDT consulting and ASNT Level III consulting for aerospace. Atlantis also runs SNT-TC-1A-based aerospace NDT training; that is not NAS 410 training, and only your Responsible Level 3 can decide whether any part of it counts toward a NAS 410 certification.

What to send us

  • The audit notice or the customer's audit request, with the date and the methods in scope.
  • Your current written practice and the Responsible Level 3 designation.
  • The NDT procedures and technique sheets for the methods being audited.
  • A list of certified personnel by method and level, and the full files for three or four of them.
  • Outside agency agreements, if you use any.
  • The purchase-order quality clauses and specifications that invoke NAS 410 or EN 4179.
  • Findings from your last Nadcap or customer audit and the corrective actions that closed them.

Send them through the audit documentation enquiry form; we reply within one business day. The wider record set for aerospace programmes is described under aerospace NDT compliance.

NAS 410 audit documentation by city

Local pages describe the aerospace base in each area, the audits suppliers there face and the documentation pressure points for that kind of work: Seattle, Phoenix, Los Angeles, San Diego, Hartford, Cincinnati, North Charleston, Tulsa, Dallas and Salt Lake City. Atlantis has no office in these cities; a Level III travels for the site work and the rest is handled remotely.

faq.q: Can an outside consultant like Atlantis be named as our Responsible Level 3?
faq.a: Atlantis does not serve as a Responsible Level 3 for any company. Your company designates its Responsible Level 3 in writing, either an employee or an outside agency your customers accept. Atlantis prepares and reviews the documents that person approves.

No. Each certification under NAS 410 is issued by the employing company, through the rules in its own written practice. Atlantis issues no certifications to the standard and does not grade examinations for it.

faq.q: Do you run NAS 410 training or examinations?
faq.a: No. Atlantis runs SNT-TC-1A-based training, which is not NAS 410 training. Whether any outside training or examination can be credited is decided by your Responsible Level 3, so ask that person before anyone enrols.

faq.q: What does a Nadcap NDT auditor check in personnel records?
faq.a: The auditor picks individual certifications and traces each one back to its training record and outline, experience log, examination papers, vision record and the written practice clause that allowed it. Gaps anywhere in that chain become findings. See AC7114 examination records.

faq.q: Do we have to move to Revision 6 straight away?
faq.a: The timing comes from your customers and from your written practice, not from Atlantis. Read the transition wording in Revision 6, note any deadline a customer has imposed, and move all affected documents across in a single controlled change.

faq.q: Can one written practice cover NAS 410 and EN 4179?
faq.a: It can, if it meets both standards and each certification states which standard, or both, it was issued under. Whether that approach is acceptable is your customers' call, so confirm it with them before you rely on it.

faq.q: Our Responsible Level 3 comes from an outside agency. What will the auditor want?
faq.a: The agreement with the agency, the written practice naming it, the designee's Level 3 certification in each method they approve, and evidence that the designee actually exercises control: signed approvals, reviews and decisions on file.

faq.q: We found gaps in old training records. Can you rebuild them?
faq.a: No, and nobody should. Atlantis lists each gap against the certification it affects and sets out options such as retraining, re-examination, a limitation or suspension. Your Responsible Level 3 decides, and the decision is recorded.

faq.q: Does an FAA repair station have to follow NAS 410?
faq.a: Not by name. FAA Advisory Circular 65-31B lists several acceptable standards for NDI personnel, NAS 410 among them. A repair station follows the standard named in its own manual and its customers' contracts.

faq.q: Do you review procedures against the method slash sheets?
faq.a: Yes. Atlantis reviews NDT procedures, technique sheets and process-control records against the AC7114 slash sheet for each method you hold, and prepares revisions for approval by a Level 3 certified in that method. See what auditors check in AC7114 procedures.

faq.q: Is the work done on site or remotely?
faq.a: Both. Gap review and drafting are remote, from Houston and Hyderabad. The mock audit and the job trace are done at your facility, because they depend on seeing real parts, real equipment and the people who do the work.
